page: Microsoft Azure FX2mds_v2 is a compute- and memory-intensive virtual machine instance powered by an Intel Xeon 8573C processor running at a sustained clock speed of 4.2 GHz under Microsoft Hyper-V. The instance provides 2 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 1 physical core with 2 execution threads. It is equipped with 42.0 GB of system memory, providing a high memory-to-vCPU allocation of 21.0 GB per vCPU. Ephemeral local storage is bundled as a 118 GB NVMe solid-state drive, while graphics processing is unaccelerated with zero GPUs.

Benchmark results reflect the high single-core frequency of the Xeon processor alongside the constraints of a 2-vCPU configuration. The instance achieves a top-tier Geekbench single-core score of 2355.0 and strong compression throughput, reaching 34.59 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip and 14.46 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, aggregate multi-core performance is limited by the low core count, resulting in weak Geekbench multi-core (2903.0) and poor stress-ng multi-core (2215.67) metrics. Memory bandwidth is constrained on uncached workloads, measuring 21.69 GB/sec for 256 MB reads and 14.62 GB/sec for writes, while PassMark memory performance remains average at 2118.93.

Qualitatively, the FX2mds_v2 provides substantial memory capacity and top-tier single-threaded compute density within a compact dual-thread footprint. The primary tradeoff lies in limited parallel execution capacity and modest I/O bandwidth, which curbs performance in multi-threaded compilation and heavy batch processing. This hardware profile is best aligned with memory-heavy single-threaded workloads, in-memory caching layers with moderate throughput requirements, electronic design automation (EDA) jobs, and licensing models constrained to low core counts requiring high clock rates.

Backed by 42.0 GB of system memory, the instance features an expansive ratio of 21.0 GB per vCPU alongside a bundled 118 GB local NVMe SSD. Single-threaded computational benchmarks demonstrate top-tier execution, highlighted by a Geekbench single-core result of 2355.0 and strong single-threaded gzip compression at 34.59 GB/sec. Conversely, multi-core throughput and uncached memory bandwidth remain constrained due to the two-vCPU envelope, producing modest multi-threaded benchmark results. Operating without GPU hardware, this instance delivers strong resource density for memory-demanding tasks that require high per-thread performance, including electronic design automation, low-concurrency database caches, and software environments constrained by per-core licensing.
